stem: A client with a markedly weakened immune system asks how to reduce foodborne-infection risk at home. Which instruction is most appropriate?

options.A: Use refrigerated deli meats without reheating because refrigeration alone is considered sufficient to control foodborne risk in a weakened immune system.
options.B: Choose pasteurized dairy and washed produce, but include undercooked eggs when the shells are intact and the eggs have remained refrigerated.
options.C: Choose fully cooked meat and eggs, but include raw sprouts after thorough rinsing because washing is considered adequate for this higher-risk food.
options.D: Choose fully cooked meat and eggs, pasteurized dairy, and washed produce, and heat deli meats until steaming hot or 165°F before serving them.

rationale: CDC guidance for people with weakened immune systems recommends thoroughly cooked meat and eggs, pasteurized dairy, washed produce, avoidance of raw or undercooked sprouts, and heating deli meats/cold cuts/hot dogs to 165°F or until steaming hot. Therefore D is correct. A leaves deli meats unheated, B includes undercooked eggs, and C incorrectly treats rinsing as sufficient for raw sprouts.
educational_objective: Teach immunocompromised clients evidence-based safer food choices that reduce foodborne-infection risk.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Safer Food Choices for People With Weakened Immune Systems
source_version_date: May 2, 2024; current CDC guidance as accessed 2026-08-16
source_locator: Safer food choices table — cooked meat/eggs, pasteurized dairy, washed produce, avoid raw sprouts; deli meats heated to 165°F or steaming hot.
source_claim_supported: Immunocompromised people should choose cooked/pasteurized/washed foods, avoid raw sprouts and undercooked eggs, and reheat deli meats to 165°F or steaming hot.

source_original.stem: A client with a markedly weakened immune system asks how to reduce foodborne-infection risk at home. Which instruction is most appropriate?

options.A: Use refrigerated deli meats without reheating because refrigeration alone is considered sufficient to control foodborne risk in a weakened immune system.
options.B: Choose pasteurized dairy and washed produce, but include undercooked eggs when the shells are intact and the eggs have remained refrigerated.
options.C: Choose fully cooked meat and eggs, but include raw sprouts after thorough rinsing because washing is considered adequate for this higher-risk food.
options.D: Choose fully cooked meat and eggs, pasteurized dairy, and washed produce, and heat deli meats until steaming hot or 165°F before serving them.

source_original.rationale: People with weakened immune systems have greater risk from foodborne illness. Option D is correct because CDC identifies thoroughly cooked meat and eggs, pasteurized dairy, washed produce, and reheated deli meats as safer choices. Option A is incorrect because unheated deli meats are a higher-risk choice. Option B is incorrect because undercooked eggs remain higher risk. Option C is incorrect because raw sprouts remain a higher-risk choice even after rinsing.
source_original.source_detail: CDC — Safer Food Choices for People With Weakened Immune Systems: choose pasteurized products and thoroughly cooked meat/eggs, wash produce, avoid raw sprouts and other higher-risk foods, and heat deli meats/hot dogs until steaming hot or 165°F when recommended for people with weakened immune systems. Current CDC food-safety guidance for people with weakened immune systems; live federal source rechecked 2026-08-15. Blueprint corrected from Basic Care and Comfort to Safety & Infection Prevention and Control because the tested objective is prevention of foodborne infection in a highly susceptible client. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: patient identification, specimen collection, asepsis, high-alert medication safeguards, fall prevention and communication that prevents safety events as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained original construct/key; the 165°F/steaming-hot deli-meat instruction is directly supported by CDC and therefore allowed precision.

audit_findings.claim_audit: All food-safety claims and 165°F deli-meat threshold are directly CDC-supported.

distractor_audit.C: Raw sprouts remain riskier despite rinsing

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only D contains no high-risk food choice.
audit_findings.cueing: All options combine multiple food choices.
